GOAL: orient in the workspace before proposing; find any frozen protocol / RQ-VAE code references.
READ: top-level directory listing only.
OBSERVED: (see tool result).
OPEN: whether a Stage3 config or RQ-VAE source is readable to anchor cost constants.

GOAL: choose a coupling position not already occupied by rounds 20261028/20261029 (which used behaviour to move codebook centroids: Poincare-Frechet successor codebook, CURVCTRL level curvature, BRad radial assignment, behcone prefix cones, branchcurv MoE, Lorentz successor-profile smoothing, succboost).
READ: only progress.jsonl exists in the workspace (no repo source readable); design therefore anchored on the frozen constants given in the task (24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch -> batch ~1023, 3000 epochs, L=3 RQ levels assumed default).
OBSERVED/REASONED: every earlier idea acts on the FORWARD quantizer (assignment rule, codebook location, curvature per level, cone aperture, residual shift). The untouched part of the design space is the BACKWARD path: the straight-through estimator that carries the quantizer gradient into the encoder. In a negatively curved latent, transporting a tangent vector along two different geodesics between the same endpoints differs by a holonomy rotation proportional to the enclosed area x curvature, so a behaviour-defined intermediate waypoint can be inserted into the gradient path and the difference it makes is a pure curvature effect (identically zero when curvature -> 0). That gives an honest three-switch coupling: curvature off -> identity, behaviour off (waypoint = item itself) -> the two legs cancel exactly.
CHOSEN: SUCC-PT-STE, parallel-transported straight-through gradient whose intermediate waypoint is the hyperbolic Karcher mean of the item's popularity-adjusted training successors.
STILL OPEN: exact per-step FLOP/wall-clock overhead (~2-4% estimated) and whether the holonomy angle is large enough to move prefix assignments; both are measured in the single run, not by ablation.

FINAL ANSWER (complete, stands alone):
IDEA: SUCC-PT-STE
TITLE: Behaviour-waypoint parallel-transported straight-through gradient for the hyperbolic RQ-VAE residual quantizer
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE SIDs are learnt from item content only; the straight-through estimator copies the quantizer gradient straight back to the encoder, so nothing in the backward path ever tells the encoder that an item should sit near the items that actually follow it. The coarse prefixes therefore cut the catalogue along content axes rather than behavioural ones, and the Stage 3 generator cannot predict the first prefix token from history.
NOVELTY: Every earlier idea here (successor-weighted Frechet codebook updates, per-level feedback curvature, behaviour-ranked radial assignment, prefix cones, branch-curvature MoE, Lorentz profile smoothing) changes the FORWARD quantizer. SUCC-PT-STE changes the BACKWARD path: the quantizer gradient is parallel-transported along a two-leg geodesic whose intermediate waypoint is the item's successor Karcher mean. Because parallel transport is path dependent only under curvature, the mechanism is inert both when curvature -> 0 (flat transport = identity = plain STE) and when the waypoint collapses to the item itself (the two legs cancel exactly). No extra parameters, no extra loss term, no coupling weight.
CHANGE: The encoder gradient for every residual level is the quantization gradient transported from the chosen code to the behaviour waypoint and then from that waypoint to the encoder output, instead of being copied unchanged; the waypoint is the hyperbolic Karcher mean of the item's popularity-adjusted training successors.
SPECIFICATION: Ball D_c={x: c||x||^2<1}, fixed curvature -c^2, lambda_x=1-c||x||^2, Mobius add oplus, gyration gyr[a,b]w. One variant only: z_i=E(e_i); forward RQ with Poincare assignment d_c and Euclidean residuals exactly as baseline; backward g_i^l=dL/dq_i^l; encoder receives G_i^l=PT_{y_i->z_i}(PT_{q_i^l->y_i}(g_i^l)) summed over l=1..L, where y_i is the frozen successor Karcher mean. c is measured once (95th percentile latent radius of the initialised encoder), anchors refresh every 50 epochs (K=2 Karcher iterations), no tuned constants.
COST: Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch => batch ~1023, L=3 levels, d=64): 1023*3*2=6138 parallel transports, each ~4 Mobius additions of dim 64 ~ 1e3 FLOP, i.e. ~6 MFLOP extra per step and ~24k extra Mobius ops, well under 2% of a step; anchor refresh every 50 epochs costs ~0.3 GFLOP each (60 refreshes in total, a couple of minutes). Overall wall clock +2-4%, no new parameters, no extra forward pass, no extra memory beyond one (24556, d) anchor table and one successor list.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping iff the curvature-induced difference between the transported gradient and the plain STE is nonzero and systematic (mean holonomy angle >> 0 on items with successors) and it moves items toward their successors' code neighbourhoods, which should show as (i) changed level-1 code usage and prefix counts, (ii) lower train-side conditional entropy H(sid_1(next)|sid_1(last)) and higher prefix-transition predictability, (iii) Stage 3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: G is not the gradient of any loss, so the encoder update is biased and reconstruction/first-level assignment can degrade; holonomy may be tiny if successors cluster near the item or near the origin, making the coupling inert; anchors computed from a drifting encoder may go stale be

tween refreshes; the successor graph is popularity-dominated, so many items could be pushed into one prefix region and lose distinguishability, which would show directly as lower Stage 3 recall.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted directed transition weights w_ij of the item-transition graph, and each item's successor Karcher mean (sequential co-consumption / directed item transitions).
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage 2 TRAIN split only, all user histories are scanned once before epoch 1; directed counts n_ij of consecutive (and window-3) item pairs are accumulated, out-degree d_i and in-degree d_j are counted, and w_ij = n_ij / sqrt(d_i * d_j); for each item i the top-20 successors by w_ij (documented cap, not tuned) and normalised weights v_ij = w_ij / sum_j w_ij are stored; empty successor sets are stored as empty and fall back to the identity.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition graph, the weight table and the anchors are built exclusively from Stage 2 training sequences, are frozen before the first Stage 2 epoch, and are never recomputed from validation or test interactions; the SID table is assigned once for all items and then frozen for Stage 3, so no test-time interaction can alter an item's semantic ID; the signal is per-item, never per-evaluation-user, so no target of a held-out session enters the construction.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare-ball parallel transport PT_{u->v}(w) = (lambda_u/lambda_v) * gyr[v, (-u)] * w in the ball of fixed curvature -c^2 with c=(0.9/R_95)^2 measured from the initialised encoder; the composition of two transports about a behaviour waypoint, whose discrepancy from the direct transport is exactly the holonomy rotation of the geodesic triangle (q_i^l, y_i, z_i).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the backward pass of every residual-quantization level at every Stage 2 training step, i.e. it rewrites the straight-through estimator of the quantizer; it also sets the forward assignment metric (Poincare distance to codes) and the Karcher-mean anchor arithmetic.
COUPLING PATH: successor table -> per-item hyperbolic Karcher waypoint y_i -> two-leg parallel transport of the level-l quantization gradient through y_i -> encoder gradient -> encoder parameters -> latent z -> all level-l prefixes. Removing the behaviour (y_i:=z_i) makes the two legs cancel and the transported gradient equals the direct curved transport, so the successor statistics change nothing; removing the curvature (c->0) makes PT the identity, so the same path returns the plain STE whatever the waypoint is.
COUPLING EQUATION: G_i^l = PT_{y_i -> z_i}( PT_{q_i^l -> y_i}( g_i^l ) ), with y_i = Karcher_{D_c}( {z_j : (i->j), v_ij} ) and PT_{u->v}(w) = (lambda_u/lambda_v) gyr[v, (-u)] w, lambda_x = 1 - c||x||^2; the encoder surrogate gradient is sum_l G_i^l in place of sum_l g_i^l.
OBSERVABLES: nonzero mean holonomy angle between G_i^l and PT_{q_i^l->z_i}(g_i^l) (zero by construction when either switch is off); changed level-1/level-2/level-3 code usage and prefix counts against the frozen baseline SID table; lower train-side conditional entropy H(sid_1(next)|sid_1(last)) and higher prefix-transition top-1 predictability; not-identical encoder parameter trajectory from the first step; final Stage 3 test_recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: y_i := z_i for every item, so the two legs cancel exactly and the encoder receives the direct curved transport PT_{q_i^l->z_i}(g_i^l); the successor table is still computed and still used nowhere else (code present, corre

ct, not trained).
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c -> 0, lambda -> 1, gyr -> identity, PT -> identity, Poincare distance -> Euclidean distance, so G_i^l = g_i^l (plain STE) and the waypoint has no effect; the successor table is still built (code present, correct, not trained).
ABLATION BOTH ON: full mechanism, y_i from the successor Karcher mean, c = (0.9/R_95)^2, G_i^l = PT_{y_i->z_i}(PT_{q_i^l->y_i}(g_i^l)); this is the single trained run of this round.
SPEC EQUATIONS: c = (0.9/R_95)^2 with R_95 = 95th percentile of ||E(e_i)|| over all 24556 items, measured once with the initialised encoder before epoch 1 and then frozen. lambda_x = 1 - c||x||^2. x oplus y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2)x + (1-c||x||^2)y)/(1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2); (-x) = -x; gyr[a,b]w = (-(a oplus b)) oplus (a oplus (b oplus w)). d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-u) oplus v||). log_u(v) = d_c(u,v) * (v oplus (-u)) / (||v oplus (-u)|| + 1e-12). Anchor (precomputed, refreshed every 50 epochs): m <- z_i; repeat K=2 times: m <- exp_m( mean_j v_ij * log_m(z_j) ) over j in Succ(i) (j != i, weights renormalised over j != i); y_i <- m if Succ(i) non-empty else z_i. Forward (unchanged from baseline apart from the metric): r_i^1 = z_i; k*_l = argmin_k d_c(r_i^l, C_l[k]); q_i^l = C_l[k*_l]; r_i^{l+1} = r_i^l - q_i^l (Euclidean residual, as baseline); L = L_recon + L_codebook + beta*L_commit, beta at the frozen baseline value. Backward override for the encoder path only: G_i^l = PT_{y_i->z_i}( PT_{q_i^l->y_i}( g_i^l ) ) with g_i^l = dL/dq_i^l; codebook and commitment gradients are left untouched. Switch implementation: BEH_OFF sets y_i = z_i at anchor construction; GEO_OFF sets c = 0 and replaces PT by the identity and d_c by the Euclidean distance; both flags read once at start-up.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder output z_i (batch, d) of the 24556 training items, codebooks C_l (L levels), frozen successor lists and normalised weights, curvature c, the two boolean switches. Outputs: the per-item per-level transported encoder gradient sum_l G_i^l (batch, d) that replaces the STE copy, and the per-item waypoint table y (24556, d) used by it.
SAFEGUARDS: clip every ball point to radius 0.99/sqrt(c) after each Mobius operation (also guarantees lambda_x >= 1 - 0.9801 > 0); add 1e-12 to every geodesic denominator and 1e-7 inside artanh with its argument clipped to 1-1e-7; because PT is an isometry of the curved metric, ||G_i^l|| is exactly ||g_i^l|| in that metric, so the mechanism cannot inflate the gradient norm and no rescaling is needed; fall back to the identity transport when ||log_{z_i}(y_i)||_c < 1e-6 or when the successor set is empty; global gradient-norm clip at the frozen baseline value stays in force; anchors are frozen for 50 epochs and rebuilt in no_grad to avoid a second backward through the graph; a NaN in any Mobius denominator triggers the identity transport for that element only, so a numerical failure degrades to the baseline instead of killing the run.
END IDEA
